own_scenes.desc: Desde su nacimiento, la crítica de rock (Rolling Stone, Creem, Los Angeles Times) trata el heavy como música de idiotas: «pimply, prole, putrid», ruido sin sutileza ni inteligencia, Black Sabbath como cuatro cavernícolas que han encontrado el equipo de una banda. Lester Bangs es la única firma notable que le concede algo, y aun así lo define como «nihilismo tecnológico». Weinstein abre el libro con este catálogo de desprecios porque coincide con el de sus enemigos del otro extremo: la crítica liberal y la derecha religiosa no se ponen de acuerdo en qué condenar, pero sí en condenarlo, y eso es lo que despierta el interés sociológico del libro.

notes.chapter: Cap. 7: Difamar la música: los detractores del metal
notes.text: La crítica de rock, nacida con la contracultura en 1967, recibe a Sabbath y Zeppelin como una afrenta personal: música «primitiva» y letras estúpidas y sexistas. Solo Lester Bangs (que llamó a Sabbath «el John Milton del rock and roll»), Robert Palmer y Jon Pareles, del New York Times, se apartan del linchamiento. Para el académico Ellis Cashmore el metal es «un dinosaurio de la cultura juvenil», apático en política. Weinstein ve en ese rechazo una lógica ideológica: los progresistas solo admiten el rock comprometido o el pop comercial, y el metal no es ninguno de los dos; su pecado es haber roto la fe de la contracultura (cambiar el amor por el mal) y su parentesco con el existencialismo, que no confía en la acción colectiva. La acusación de simpleza no resiste la notación que necesita una guitarra de metal.

refs.q: Lester Bangs, the only noted rock critic who had anything favorable to say about heavy metal at its inception
refs.para: Lester Bangs, the only noted rock critic who had anything favorable to say about heavy metal at its inception, writes some years later: “As its detractors have always claimed, heavy-metal rock is nothing more than a bunch of noise; it is not music, it’s distortion—and that is precisely why its adherents find it appealing. Of all contemporary rock, it is the genre most closely identified with violence and aggression, rapine and carnage. Heavy metal orchestrates technological nihilism.”¹⁰
refs.chapter: Cap. 1: Estudiar el metal: el bricolage de la cultura

refs.q: The severity of the denunciations directed at heavy metal and the disagreement exhibited by its two major opponents, the liberal-left rock critics and the religious right
refs.para: The severity of the denunciations directed at heavy metal and the disagreement exhibited by its two major opponents, the liberal-left rock critics and the religious right, concerning what to denounce are enough to pique a sociologist’s interest. Why should a style of music have occasioned such extravagant rhetoric, not only from members of the lunatic fringe, but also from responsible elements on both sides of the political spectrum? Can a form of music that has attracted millions of fans for more than twenty years be all that dangerous? Does a form of music warrant being placed along with a dread disease (AIDS) and drug abuse? Are the critics of heavy metal really talking about music? If not, what is it that they are talking about?
refs.chapter: Cap. 1: Estudiar el metal: el bricolage de la cultura

refs.q: He upped his rhetorical comparisons by stating that the group was “the John Milton of rock ‘n’ roll.”
refs.para: In his 1972 analysis of Black Sabbath, Lester Bangs concurred with Butler, remarking that the critics reacted as one in damning the band.⁶ Bangs was one of the few rock critics who, at least initially, did not join the metal-bashing bandwagon. He argued that Sabbath were moralists, like Bob Dylan and the novelist William Burroughs. He upped his rhetorical comparisons by stating that the group was “the John Milton of rock ‘n’ roll.”⁷ Critics Robert Palmer and Jon Pareles of the New York Times have also been exceptions to the rule of metal bashing. Palmer has argued that the “darker” kinds of metal, like other horror genres in popular culture, simply reflect the anxieties and problems of the society at large.⁸
refs.chapter: Cap. 7: Difamar la música: los detractores del metal

refs.q: At the root of the progressive critic’s special contempt for heavy metal is the fact that it broke the faith of the counterculture.
refs.para: At the root of the progressive critic’s special contempt for heavy metal is the fact that it broke the faith of the counterculture. Black Sabbath, in particular, self-consciously inverted the counterculture’s central symbol of love. Instead of focusing on love, they sang about evil, pointing out its pervasiveness and playing with its value sign. Heavy metal does not celebrate “love,” either as something that is or should be the basis of sociopolitical relationships, although the spirit of community and sharing does inform many of the practices of the heavy metal subculture. Until recently, and then only in punk-influenced thrash, political reformism was alien to metal lyrics. The audience for metal is unhip. The notion of being politically correct is completely alien to its members. They are rock-and-roll rebels with a taste for Dionysian pleasure. They have judgments on politics, but those judgments do not involve programs of collective action.
